dedupe_keys.name: aixdhn district heating networks dataset from clustered census data

description: AixDHN contains inferred district-heating areas for Germany, with annual residential heat demand, demand density, household counts and administrative identifiers. RWTH Aachen University’s Institute for Energy Efficient Buildings and Indoor Climate publishes the dataset to identify district-heating grids from clustered census and demand data. The repository lists one GeoJSON file for each of the 16 German states. Spatial objects are polygons of presumed heating networks, with centroids and census-cell membership in EPSG:3035. The documentation does not state the census reference year or a regular update schedule. The data are available directly in the public GitHub repository under the MIT licence, so access and reuse are free. The accompanying paper is linked in the README. A limitation is that inferred service areas do not establish actual pipe alignments or hydraulic connectivity. Annual residential demand also does not supply hourly operating profiles or non-residential loads. Simulation uses include district-heating capacity planning and optimisation of possible supply areas before constructing a detailed network model. The dataset complements data-hotmaps-building-stock-and-heat-density-maps as a separate source for heat-demand comparisons; compatibility has not been tested.
